• Every slide lives in content/slides.json — the single source of truth.
  • Text blocks hold HTML; component blocks reference interactive modules by name.
  • Claude edits the JSON and drops component files into components/; you edit the same JSON through the point-and-click editor.
  • Both authoring paths converge on one file, so nothing gets clobbered.

slides.notes: The key architectural idea: because slides are data, programmatic edits (Claude) and manual edits (the inline editor) are just two writers of the same JSON.

• Click any text to edit it in place. Hover a block for move, delete, and component-props controls.
  • The toolbar adds, duplicates, reorders, and deletes slides and blocks.
  • Save writes straight to content/slides.json when the dev server is running — otherwise it downloads the file for you to drop in.
  • A draft is kept in your browser, so nothing is lost between sessions.

blocks.html:
The whole deck is static files — no build step. Connect the repo to Netlify once, and every push publishes. Viewers see a clean presentation; ?edit stays your secret door.

See the README for the two-minute setup, and for the conventions Claude follows when adding slides and components in your content projects.
